en.def: A set of database transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability. Iceberg provides ACID semantics over commodity object stores.

tr.def: Veritabanı işlemlerinde dört garanti: atomiklik, tutarlılık, izolasyon, dayanıklılık. Iceberg bu garantileri nesne depolama üzerinde sunar.

en.def: Multi-Version Concurrency Control. Readers see a consistent snapshot while writers create new versions; no read locks. Iceberg snapshots are the multi-version mechanism.
Open table format for huge analytic datasets. Snapshot-based, schema-evolution-safe, engine-agnostic.
Apache Spark — distributed compute engine for large-scale data processing. Reads and writes Iceberg natively.
Apache Flink — stream-first distributed processing engine. Iceberg integration via Flink connector.
Apache Paimon — streaming lakehouse format. Designed for low-latency stream-table convergence.
A metadata store that maps table names to current Iceberg metadata files. REST, Hive, Glue, Nessie are common implementations.
An immutable, point-in-time view of an Iceberg table. Every write creates a new snapshot. Time travel is just reading an older snapshot.
Merging many small data files into fewer larger ones. Reduces read overhead and metadata size; tunable in Iceberg via maintenance procedures.
Querying a table as it existed at a past snapshot or timestamp. Reads are still cheap because Iceberg metadata makes the lookup an O(log) hop, not a scan.
